newsitem.title: USA: Knoxville, Tenn., airport seeks renovation bonds.
newsitem.headline: Knoxville, Tenn., airport seeks renovation bonds.

text.p: Tennessee's McGhee Tyson Airport is expected to undergo a $40 million terminal renovation financed with bonds, an aviation official said Wednesday.

"We have got an open bond resolution that is used to finance improvements by adding additional series. Our intent is to ask the city of Knoxville to issue a series of double-barreled bonds," said Terry Igoe, executive director of the Metropolitan Knoxville Airport Authority.
The bonds would be backed with revenues from airport rents and a passenger facility charge. They would carry a secondary pledge from the city's general obligation taxing power.
The airport authority could raise rents by 5 percent to help pay debt service if necessary. But, Igoe said, "We believe we'll be able to repay the bonds with our existing rate base."
It would be the first time the authority has used a passenger facility fee to finance terminal improvements.
The 230,000-square foot terminal is 24 years old and serves 1.5 million pasengers a year, a number that has grown by an average of 4.2 percent a year for the past 10 years.
The project is in the design phase. Construction bids will be opened in the spring but no date has been set for the bond issue, Igoe said.
"We probably wouldn't go to the market until we need the funds," he said.

A revamped terminal is expected to be completed by the spring of 2000. The authority last issued bonds in May 1993, when it took on $5.3 millon in debt to build an addition to a parking garage. The bonds will be paid off in 2012.
